name: TX-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: Deeply Republican district with R+23 partisan lean
Jackson's massive financial advantage ($5.4M cash vs $14K)
Incumbent running with no expert raters flagging the race
Markets price Jackson at ~94% to win
model.rationale: The R+23 district, Ronny Jackson's incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage make this safely Republican; Polymarket prices him around 94%. Nair's minimal fundraising gives no evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected incumbent retirement could open the door, but nothing in the current evidence suggests movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 13th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+23. Incumbent Ronny Jackson is running for reelection and holds an overwhelming financial edge, with more than $5.4 million on hand compared to roughly $14,000 for Democratic challenger Mark Nair, who has raised about $102,000. Outside spending also favors Jackson, and no outside groups are opposing him.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, but prediction markets give Jackson roughly a 94% chance of winning. With no signs of competition, the seat is expected to remain comfortably in Republican hands in November.
